script: Good morning, and welcome to your market briefing for Friday 25 September. We start in New York, where our watchlist leaned lower. Nvidia was the weakest name, down one point four seven percent to about two hundred and twenty six US dollars, and it did that on lighter than usual turnover, around zero point seven times average volume. Apple eased zero point eight percent to about three hundred and thirty seven dollars. Meta has put Apple in its sights with new virtual reality glasses, according to one report on the day. JPMorgan Chase slipped zero point seven three percent, also near three hundred and thirty seven dollars, with volume a touch above average. Chief executive Jamie Dimon said artificial intelligence spending could reach a trillion dollars in twenty twenty seven. On the other side, Microsoft added zero point five two percent to just over five hundred dollars, and Tesla rose zero point three two percent to about three hundred and eighty dollars. So, a mixed and fairly quiet session overall. Now to London. The tone there was also uneven. Vodafone was the standout decliner, down two point one five percent to about one hundred and twenty five pence, on one point four times its average volume. HSBC fell one point five nine percent to roughly fifteen hundred and nine pence, and the bank was reported to be targeting younger workers with an entry level hiring drive. BP was essentially flat, down zero point one one percent near five hundred and forty two pence, on light turnover. The gainers came from the defensive end. Unilever rose one point two percent to about forty seven hundred pence, with a McCormick food deal facing a United Kingdom competition review. AstraZeneca added zero point eight nine percent to around twelve thousand six hundred and seventy pence, on one and a half times average volume, which is unusual. Its Trixeo treatment secured approval for asthma in the European Union. Looking to our own region, the lead from offshore is a cautious one. The Australian market opens at ten o'clock Eastern time, with local futures pointing to a flat to slightly positive start. At half past eleven we get quarterly Australian job vacancies data from the statistics bureau, watched for signs of a cooling labour market. Miners are in focus all day, with overnight iron ore and copper moves setting the tone for BHP, Rio Tinto and Fortescue. Across the Tasman, the New Zealand trade balance lands at a quarter to nine, before the local market opens. This briefing is AI-generated general information only. It is not financial advice.
